subject: Retention granularities for prompts, responses and session fragments — residency & deletion clarification
messages:

Subject: Clarify default retention windows and EU residency for prompts/outputs

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As we evaluate Redwood for our assistant pilot, procurement asked for a short, unambiguous summary of what Redwood keeps by default and where that data is stored. Specifically we need to know: 

- Default retention windows (by default) for: raw requests/prompts, model responses (final outputs), streamed fragments (intermediate tokens), and any KV cache/session artifacts.
- Whether hosted requests from EU users are kept in-region (EU) by default, and how residency is guaranteed (regions/locations).
- Deletion/erasure SLA if we request a purge of our account data (how long, what evidence do you provide).

We need a bulleted summary we can paste into the SOW and a short attachment for procurement — ideally a single-sheet matrix they can sign off on. Can you put something together this week?

Cheers,
Liam

Hi Liam —

Thanks — note attached: a concise retention matrix (retention_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a one-page deletion runbook summary (deletion_runbook_summary.pdf). High level answers below; the attachments include the exact wording procurement prefers.

Summary (default behavior unless customer configures otherwise):
- Raw requests/prompts: retained for 7 days by default. Short-term storage is used for routing/queueing and diagnostics; not indexed for search.
- Final model responses/outputs: retained for 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring.
- Streamed/intermediate fragments: buffered in memory for up to 2 hours during the streaming session and not written to long-term logs by default.
- KV cache / session state: ephemeral by default (cleared at session end) and not persisted beyond 24 hours unless explicitly pinned by the customer.
- Derivatives (embeddings, reranking artifacts): treated as customer artifacts; default retention 365 days unless customer overrides.

Residency:
- EU-hosted requests are stored in the eu-central-1 region by default. The control plane notes the region and we provide region-scoped logs. For Dedicated/Private deployments, residency follows the customer's VPC region.

Deletion/erasure SLA:
- Ad hoc deletion requests via console or support ticket begin a purge workflow. For hosted accounts: deletion pipeline executes within 72 hours; full proof-of-deletion (exportable audit log) available within 7 business days. Private deployments follow customer-managed deletion controls; we provide guidance and deletion scripts.

Next steps: I added Kimberly and Karthik to the thread to confirm technical details around buffering and proof-of-deletion artifacts. If that matches what procurement needs, tell me how you want the phrasing in the SOW and we will provide a procurement-ready paragraph.

Attachments: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (single-sheet matrix), deletion_runbook_summary.pdf (2 pages).

Best,
Priyom

Liam / team —

Adding technical precision to Priyom's summary so procurement has exact language: 

- Prompts (raw requests): these are written to a short-lived request store and purged by a daily compaction job. Default retention window is 7 days; purge jobs mark records tombstoned and then a background deletion job removes them from object storage within 24–48 hours of tombstone.

- Final outputs: stored in our customer artifact bucket with lifecycle policy; default TTL is 30 days. Customers can set a shorter TTL at the project level or enable a "no-store" flag at request time which prevents final outputs from being written.

- Streamed fragments: streaming uses a transient buffer service. Nothing is written to persistent logs unless the request finishes and writes an output artifact. The buffer keeps up to 2 hours of fragments for reconnect/resume semantics; those buffers are scoped to the session and scrubbed asynchronously after session close.

- KV cache/session artifacts: ephemeral by default. In hosted plans the default is to keep session KV for up to 24 hours to allow short-lived sessions to resume; Dedicated customers can configure longer or disable persistence entirely. Pinned KV (explicit API call) is stored as a customer artifact and follows artifact retention rules.

- Derivatives: embeddings and indexes are customer artifacts; we do not persist derivatives on behalf of Redwood unless the customer uses our managed index product. Default 365-day TTL, configurable.

- Residency guarantees: for EU customers we operate isolated storage in eu-central-1 and do not replicate customer-managed artifacts to other regions unless the customer opts in. Audit evidence includes S3 bucket location, access logs, and a signed deletion manifest.

- Proof-of-deletion: our runbook produces a deletion manifest (object ids, timestamps) and an audit log entry. For hosted customers we provide a signed manifest and internal deletion-trace logs within 7 business days. For high-assurance requests we can perform an on-demand scan and provide SHA256 checksum verification of deleted objects (adds ~2 business days).

If you want, Marissa can convert the two attachments into procurement language that we can paste into a contract clause.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
